cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, written for the choirmaster with stringed instruments. David is talking straight to the LORD, and friend, this is not a happy little tune. He opens with, "O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger or discipline me in Your wrath."

cards.question: David keeps going with his next request. What does he ask the LORD to show him?
David tells the LORD he's strong enough to get through this on his own.

cards.text: David tells the LORD he's frail and his bones are in agony.

cards.question: David says it isn't only his bones that hurt. His soul is deeply distressed too.

cards.text: Then David cries out, "How long, O LORD, how long?"
Then David asks the LORD to turn, deliver his soul and save him. Short prayer. BIG ask.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to save him. What reason does David give?

cards.text: David gives the LORD one more reason to save him. And this one has to do with death.

cards.question: David says the dead in Sheol keep right on praising the LORD.

cards.text: Now David tells the LORD he's weary from groaning. Friend, when even the GROANING wears you out, you are TIRED.

cards.question: David says his weeping goes on all night long.

cards.text: He floods his bed with weeping and drenches his couch with tears. Friend, forget a towel: that couch needs a LIFEGUARD.

cards.question: After all that weeping through the night, what does David say is happening to his eyes?

cards.text: His eyes grow dim because of all his foes. Then the whole song FLIPS, and the same David who was drenching his couch tells all the workers of iniquity to depart from him.

cards.question: David suddenly tells the workers of iniquity to get away from him. What does he say has changed?

answers.text: The LORD has heard his weeping
His tears have finally dried up
His army has just shown up

cards.question: David is sure the LORD has heard his weeping. So now David says his prayer has been ___ by the LORD.

cards.text: The LORD has heard David's cry for mercy, and He accepts his prayer. Friend, I KNOW that switch: years in the dark of a junk drawer, and then one night the light pours in.

cards.question: Now David looks at all his enemies. What does he say will happen to them?

answers.text: They will turn back in disgrace
They will win in the end

cards.text: His enemies will be ashamed and dismayed, turning back in sudden disgrace like somebody who just walked into the wrong meeting.
